judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Material" sweeps in "any progeny, portions, unmodified derivatives and any accompanying know-how or data," terms whose boundary (especially "unmodified derivatives" and "know-how") is genuinely contestable when Recipient builds a new lentiviral construct from the transferred sequence. The final sentence's reservation of rights "including any altered forms of the Material made by St. Jude" is an odd carve-out that invites argument about altered forms made by Recipient.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Paragraph 8, which lets Recipient patent inventions "made by Recipient through use of the Material" and grants St. Jude only a non-commercial license back, the no-implied-licenses sentence here pulls toward St. Jude retaining rights in anything containing Material, creating real tension over ownership of the derived construct. Paragraph 7's "no rights other than those specifically set forth" compounds the same question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single sentence functions as both a permission and a limit, and it is unclear whether "only" restricts the purpose of use or also the downstream use of the resulting lentiviral construct, and whether "pre-clinical studies" bars later clinical translation of the derived construct. The absence of any definition of the derived construct's status leaves the scope of the restriction genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4 forbids human use and any commercial purpose while Paragraph 8 expressly contemplates commercialization with approval and patent filings, so the pre-clinical-only limit here must be harmonised with a clause anticipating products; that is a live reconciliation problem. Paragraph 1's broad "Material" definition also affects whether the newly created construct falls inside this restriction.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 3 — Permitted use of Material (2003 MTA)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains a plain mechanical error ("raw-exclusive" for non-exclusive) and a barely legible handwritten interlineation apparently addressing inventorship under U.S. patent law, whose text and effect cannot be read with confidence. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, unambiguous reservation that St. Jude may distribute the Material to other entities; "unrestricted" is emphatic rather than uncertain. No enumerated list or catch-all creates scope doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the undefined "collaborative research study" from the preamble, but no operative clause contradicts a joint-publication duty. Consistent enough with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The termination-at-will on thirty days' notice and the duty to destroy unused Materials are clear; the text is definite apart from scanning noise interposed mid-sentence. "No rights other than those specifically set forth" is a standard reservation.
